rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis studies a compositional change (adding Ta, Nb, V to HfZrTi) in a bulk alloy, while the hidden target applies an AlCoCrFeNi coating via atmospheric plasma spraying and annealing. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses as-cast alloys, quasi-static and dynamic compression in air, while the target uses APS deposition, annealing, microhardness, electrochemical testing in H2SO4, and hot-corrosion cycling in molten salts at 900 °C. The conditions share no common regime.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes BCC stabilization, solid-solution strengthening, and adiabatic-shear-induced oxidation for energy release. The target relies on grain refinement, BCC phase, high-entropy sluggish diffusion, and formation of Cr/Al-rich passive oxides for corrosion resistance. These are entirely different classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts increased strength, ductility, and dynamic oxidation sparking relative to HZTX0. The target predicts higher microhardness, better electrochemical corrosion resistance, and lower hot-corrosion weight gain relative to uncoated SS316L. The properties and directions are unrelated.
